31: Tell me who you are, you of the fierce form. Homage to you, best of gods. Be gracious. I want to know you fully, you who are the first one, for I do not understand what you are doing.
32: I am time, fully grown, the destroyer of the worlds, set in motion here to draw the worlds in. Even without you, all the warriors standing in the opposing armies will cease to be.
33: So stand up and win fame. Conquer your enemies and enjoy a prosperous kingdom. I alone have already struck these men down. Be merely the instrument, you who shoot with the left hand too.
34: Droṇa, Bhīṣma, Jayadratha, Karṇa and the other heroic warriors as well have been slain by me: you, slay them. Do not be shaken. Fight. You will conquer your rivals in battle.
35: When he heard these words of Keśava, the crowned one joined his palms, trembling, and paid homage. Then, bowing down and very frightened, he spoke to Kṛṣṇa again in a stammering voice.
36: It is right, Hṛṣīkeśa, that the world rejoices in praising you and is filled with love. The demons run off in fear in all directions, and all the hosts of perfected ones pay homage.
37: And why should they not bow to you, great self, the first maker, greater even than Brahmā? Endless one, lord of the gods, abode of the world, you are the imperishable, the existent, the non-existent and what is beyond that.
38: You are the first god, the ancient person. You are the supreme resting place of this universe. You are the knower, what is to be known and the supreme abode. The universe is pervaded by you, you of endless form.
39: You are Vāyu, Yama, Agni, Varuṇa, the moon, the lord of creatures and the great-grandfather. Homage, homage to you a thousand times, and again, and yet once more, homage, homage to you.
40: Homage to you from the front and from behind. Homage to you from every side, you who are all. You of endless strength, your might is measureless. You reach through all, and so you are all.
41: Thinking of you as a friend, I have spoken rashly, calling you Kṛṣṇa, Yādava, friend. I did not know this greatness of yours, and I spoke out of carelessness or even out of affection.
42: And I have treated you without respect for the sake of a joke, at play, lying down, sitting and eating, alone or even, unfallen one, in front of others. For that I ask your forgiveness, you who are immeasurable.
43: You are the father of this world, of all that moves and all that does not, the one to be worshipped and the greater teacher. No one is equal to you. How then could there be another who surpasses you, even in the three worlds, you of matchless power?
44: So I bow down, lay my body low and ask for your grace, lord who is to be praised. As a father bears with a son, a friend with a friend, a dear one with a dear one, so you, god, ought to bear with me.
45: I am thrilled to have seen what was never seen before, and my mind is badly shaken with fear. Show me that very form, god. Be gracious, lord of the gods, abode of the world.
46: I wish to see you in just that way, wearing a crown, bearing a mace, with a discus in your hand. Take that very four-armed form, thousand-armed one, you whose shape is the universe.
47: Being gracious to you, Arjuna, I have shown you this supreme form through the yoga of the self. It is made of splendour, all-containing, endless and first, this form of mine that no one but you has seen before.
48: Not by the Vedas, sacrifices and study, not by gifts, not by rites and not by fierce austerities can I be seen in such a form in the world of men by anyone but you, great hero of the Kurus.
49: Do not be distressed and do not be bewildered at seeing this form of mine, terrible as it is. With your fear gone and your mind glad, look again at that very form of mine, this one here.
50: Having spoken so to Arjuna, Vāsudeva showed his own form once more. And the great self, gentle in body again, comforted the frightened man.
51: Now that I see this gentle human form of yours, Janārdana, I am in possession of my mind and have returned to my own nature.
52: This form of mine that you have seen is very hard to see. Even the gods are always longing for a sight of this form.
53: Not by the Vedas, not by austerity, not by giving and not by sacrifice can I be seen in the way that you have seen me.
54: But by devotion directed to no other, Arjuna, I can in this way be known and seen in truth, and entered, scorcher of foes.
55: One who does action for me, who holds me as the highest and is devoted to me, who is free from attachment and without enmity toward all beings: that one comes to me, son of Pāṇḍu.
